t.3.7.1: Rāma, together with Saumitri, honored by Sutīkṣṇa, spent the night there and awoke at daybreak.
t.3.7.2: Rising at the proper time, Rāghava, together with Sītā, performed his ablutions with very cool water fragrant with lotuses.
t.3.7.3: Then they, Vaidehī and Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, having duly worshipped at daybreak the fire and the gods in the forest that was a refuge for ascetics,
t.3.7.4: Seeing the sun rising, they, freed from all impurity, approached Sutīkṣṇa and spoke these gentle words.
t.3.7.5: O blessed one, we have dwelt here happily, honoured by you who are worthy of honour. We take our leave and shall depart, for the sages are urging us to hurry.
t.3.7.6: We are eager to see the entire circle of hermitages of the sages of virtuous conduct who dwell in the Daṇḍaka forest.
t.3.7.7: We wish to take our leave, together with these foremost of sages, who are ever devoted to dharma and subdued by austerity, like fires whose flames have died down.
t.3.7.9: "Now we wish to go," said Rāghava, and together with Saumitri and with Sītā he paid reverence to the feet of the sage.
t.3.7.8: Let us go before the sun, its heat grown unbearable, blazes too fiercely, like a man without noble lineage who has gained fortune by a wrongful path.
t.3.7.10: Raising up the two who were touching his feet, the foremost of sages embraced them tightly and with affection, and spoke these words.
t.3.7.11: Go by a safe path, O Rāma, together with Saumitri and with this Sītā, who follows you like a shadow.
t.3.7.12: Behold, O hero, the delightful hermitage of these ascetics who dwell in the Daṇḍaka forest, whose souls have been purified by austerity.
t.3.7.14: Ponds and lakes with clusters of full-blown lotuses and clear, tranquil waters, scattered over with kāraṇḍava ducks.
t.3.7.13: the flowering forests, rich in abundant fruits and roots, with their tranquil herds of deer and peaceful flocks of birds.
t.3.7.15: You will see mountain streams and springs delightful to the eye, and lovely forests resounding with the cries of peacocks.
t.3.7.17: Thus addressed, Kākutstha, together with Lakṣmaṇa, said "So be it," and having circumambulated the sage, keeping him to his right, he set about to depart.
t.3.7.16: Go, dear child, and you too, Saumitri, may go. Having seen all this, you must come back once again to my hermitage.
t.3.7.18: Then the large-eyed Sītā gave the two brothers their splendid quivers and bows, and then their spotless swords.
t.3.7.19: Having fastened on their two splendid quivers and taken up their twanging bows, both Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa went forth from the hermitage to set out on their way.
